title: 5 Things You Must Lose to Find Your Purpose
paragraphs: 5 Things You Must Lose to Find Your Purpose
You can’t carry your calling with a death grip on what God told you to surrender.
Purpose is not found by adding more.
Sometimes it is found by losing what is killing you slowly.
Here are 5 things you must lose to find your purpose:

1. Lose the need to be liked by everyone.
If your life is controlled by applause, your purpose will be buried under performance. Jesus was loved by crowds on one day and crucified by a crowd days later. Calling was never built on public approval. It was built on obedience. “Am I now trying to win the approval of human beings, or of God?” (Galatians 1:10)

2. Lose your secret sin.
You cannot walk in holy purpose while feeding hidden compromise. What you protect in darkness will sabotage what God wants to reveal in light. Some people keep asking for destiny while sleeping beside disobedience. But grace does not cover you so you can keep hiding. Grace calls you out so you can be healed. “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us…” (1 John 1:9)

3. Lose the fantasy of control.
Purpose begins where surrender starts. A lot of people do not want God’s will. They want God’s blessing on their will. But Jesus did not redeem you so you could stay on the throne of your own life. He calls you to deny yourself, take up your cross, and follow Him. (Luke 9:23)

4. Lose your old identity.
You are not your past. Not your failure. Not your addiction. Not the name they called you when you were broken. In Christ, the old has gone. The new has come. (2 Corinthians 5:17)
And that’s where grace walks in.
Purpose is not born from self-invention. It is born from new creation.

5. Lose the fear of dying empty.
Some people never start because they are afraid to fail. But a buried gift is already a failure of surrender. The safest place in the world is not comfort. It is the will of God. Better to limp in obedience than sit polished in disobedience.

You do not find your purpose by staring deeper into yourself.
You find it by looking to Christ.

Because purpose is not first about platform.
It is about repentance.
It is about redemption.
It is about belonging fully to Jesus.

At the cross, He takes what must die.
Your pride.
Your chains.
Your false self.
And from that grave, He raises a life that finally knows why it exists.

So lose what is choking your soul.
And find the Christ who gives your life its meaning.
